answers.solution:
Done. I built a faithful reproduction, verified every diagnostic step and the fix end-to-end, and wrote the deliverable to `~/gitreins-residue-solution.md` (346 lines).

## What I found

The foreman lane is blocked by an **all-or-nothing ownership barrier** firing on a **convention-less bulk copy** of judge bundles — not by work in progress. The five diagnostic facts hold: one dominant new top-level class, N byte-identical physical copies (same `sha256sum`, `links=1`, different inodes), zero live producer (no ticks, no CLI rescue code, no logs, no git writer cwd), and zero tracking convention (`git ls-files .gitreins/rescued-*` = 0, no commits). The stale `git add .gitreins/history …` recipe neither covers nor should cover it.

## Verified fix

Quarantine the class out of the worktree (reversible, no commit), keep one canonical copy for the owner, record a class-scoped ruling, and re-prove with sorted-path digests + `diff -q`. Measured on the repro:

- before: `BLOCKED: 1440 untracked .gitreins paths`
- after: `CLEAR: 0 untracked .gitreins paths`, nothing staged
- `diff -q expected==end` passed; two end censuses had identical SHA-256
- anti-pattern quantified: `git add` would have staged 1440 files / 15,937,920 bytes

Two real traps surfaced and are documented:
1. A census/ledger written **inside `.gitreins/` re-trips the barrier** (`BLOCKED: 1`) — keep scratch and rulings outside the worktree.
2. The `/proc` writer census must exclude its own process tree and match `/proc/<pid>/exe`, not argv substrings, or a wrapper shell containing "git add" false-positives.

The markdown is self-contained: root-cause analysis, the copy-paste `gitreins-residue-triage.sh` (syntax-checked against the exact script I ran), the revised fail-closed owner recipe, and a verification transcript including the observer `Scanned N files` cross-check.

signatures.description:
Diagnosis pattern for a foreman/ops lane blocked by untracked GitReins evaluator state in a repo whose closeout convention TRACKS .gitreins/history.

1) Never re-derive the census by eye. Capture once to a tick-unique scratch path, then normalize: `cut -c4- porcelain.txt | sort > paths.txt; sha256sum paths.txt`. The sorted-path SHA-256 (not the raw porcelain digest) is the only value that can prove a refire is identical, and it must be recomputed at the END of the tick and compared with `diff -q` to prove the barrier held.
2) Split the delta by depth BEFORE classifying: `cut -d/ -f1-2 paths.txt | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn`. A single new directory of tens of thousands of paths is usually a bulk copy, not work in progress.
3) Prove duplication instead of assuming it: sample one file path under two top-level trees and compare `sha256sum` plus `stat -c '%h %i'`. Byte-identical content with link count 1 and different inodes = N physical copies of one corpus; size/N is the unique payload. A 'rescue' directory that replicates the same run ids under per-task trees is this shape (measured: 686 MB, 35,854 files, 18 task trees x ~630 run dirs, unique payload ~38 MB).
4) Prove the producer out-of-band before blaming a sibling lane: no scheduler tick in the window (`ticks` table), no rescue code in the installed CLI (`grep -rn 'rescued-' <site-packages>/gitreins/`), no entry in `.gitreins/logs/`, and a `/proc/*/cwd` census over the canonical root returning zero live writers.
5) Prove the tracking convention prefix-scoped, never by substring: `git ls-files .gitreins/rescued-* | wc -l` and `git log --oneline --all -- <dir> | wc -l`. Zero on both means the class has no repo convention to protect and shrinks the owner decision from 'resolve all N paths' to named classes plus a named remainder.
6) Invalidate, then republish, the owner recipe: an `git add <dir> ...` recipe stops covering the residue the moment a new top-level class appears, and blindly widening it to a duplicated rescue tree would commit hundreds of MB of duplicate judge bundles into git history permanently. The recipe must name the new class and demand a dedupe/keep-one/ignore ruling instead of an adopt.

Cross-check the path count against a concurrent observer when one exists: a sibling lane's gitreins guard log prints 'Scanned N files', and an equal N confirms both lanes measured the same tree.
signatures.environment: linux, git 2.x checkout shared by scheduler lanes; repo tracks .gitreins/ history (2000+ files) but its history is pruned over time
